content_policy: Each card is an original project-authored synopsis and investigation checklist. The repository does not store third-party PDFs or copied passages. Source links and reuse notes are retained for review.

sources.title: Automated Driving Systems 2.0: A Vision for Safety
sources.publisher: U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
sources.reuse_basis: Official U.S. Government source. This repository stores an original synopsis only, not the publication text.
sources.summary: The safety elements provide investigation categories for automated-driving events: system safety, operational design domain, object and event detection and response, and fallback behavior. They are a review framework, not a case-level compliance verdict.
investigation_prompts: Check whether the observed event is consistent with an object-and-event detection, response, ODD, or fallback question before assigning root cause.
Record what evidence is missing before concluding that a disengagement reflects a system limitation rather than an expected fallback.
sources.limitations: Voluntary U.S. guidance for ADS; do not present it as a binding requirement for another jurisdiction or automation level.

sources.title: Open Source Surrogate Safety Assessment Model: 2017 Enhancement and Update
sources.reuse_basis: Official U.S. Government source. This repository stores an original synopsis only, not the publication text.
sources.summary: Trajectory-based conflict analysis can use surrogate measures such as time to collision, post-encroachment time, deceleration, relative speed, and delta-v. These measures support an investigation of interaction risk; they do not identify the software subsystem that caused it.
investigation_prompts: Inspect the interaction timeline around the minimum TTC, including relative speed, trajectory overlap, and any evasive maneuver.
Treat a critical surrogate metric as a safety signal and correlate it with perception, prediction, planning, and control evidence before proposing a cause.
sources.limitations: The source focuses on surrogate conflict analysis and does not validate a vehicle-control function or establish a universal threshold.

sources.title: PEGASUS Method for Scenario-Based Safety Assessment
sources.reuse_basis: Reference-only project pointer. The project page was not established as an open-content licence during this POC; this card is an original factual synopsis and does not reproduce project PDFs or website text.
sources.summary: A scenario-based review can connect measured driving data to logical scenario parameters and criticality indicators. This is useful for asking whether a disengagement belongs to a repeatable scenario family rather than treating each incident as an isolated story.
investigation_prompts: Describe the event as a repeatable logical scenario: road context, actor interaction, maneuver, timing, and criticality indicators.
Compare this case with parameter variations rather than inferring broad safety coverage from one concrete scenario.
sources.limitations: A methodology reference, not an open licence to ingest PEGASUS publications or a proof that a scenario is safe.

sources.title: Development of a Framework for Generating Driving Safety Assessment Scenarios for Automated Vehicles
sources.reuse_basis: Open-access article under CC BY 4.0. This repository stores an original synopsis with attribution rather than copied article text.
sources.summary: Safety assessment scenarios can be organised from functional intent through logical parameter ranges to concrete test instances. Layered scenario descriptions make it easier to separate road context, dynamic actors, environment, communication, and automation behavior in a review packet.
investigation_prompts: Separate what happened in this concrete replay from the logical parameters that should be varied in follow-up testing.
Document which environmental, traffic, map, and automation layers are represented and which are absent from the available telemetry.
sources.limitations: A scenario-generation framework; it does not diagnose a proprietary stack or define deployment approval criteria.

sources.title: Selecting Non-Line of Sight Critical Scenarios for Connected Autonomous Vehicle Testing
sources.publisher: Journal of Sensor and Actuator Networks (MDPI)
sources.reuse_basis: Open-access article under CC BY 4.0. This repository stores an original synopsis with attribution rather than copied article text.
sources.summary: Occlusion and non-line-of-sight interactions are useful edge-case families because safety-relevant actors may be difficult to observe until late in an interaction. Criticality should be assessed with multiple measures and scenario context, rather than one KPI in isolation.
investigation_prompts: Check whether occlusion, late observability, or uncertainty about another actor could explain the degraded perception or interaction evidence.
Compare multiple signals—visibility, perception confidence, TTC, actor motion, and prediction divergence—instead of treating one KPI as a root-cause label.
sources.limitations: Focused on a particular critical-scenario class; it is not evidence that this simulated case contains a real occlusion.
